prerequisites: Basics of component modeling and drawing creation with CAD.
Knowledge and calculation of selected machine elements such as shaft-hub connections, screw connections, and welded connections.

learning_outcomes.text: Assess and purposefully apply methods and systematics for creating CAD models.
Select and practically use a commercially available associative-parametric 3D-CAD system.
Develop, implement, and evaluate efficient and user-appropriate modeling strategies for the later reuse of models in the sense of CAx and master this basic model reuse.
Purposefully use commercially available CAD systems.
Master the creation of parametric solid modeling including the creation of meaningful reference geometry, CSG, and B-Rep objects.
Master the technique of sweeping, also for the creation of freeform surfaces.
Know the CAD program structure.
Identify and classify program parts.
Master fundamental mathematical algorithms (projections, solvers, etc.) and use them for error analysis.
Know common CAD interface formats and their advantages and disadvantages.
Select and evaluate CAD interface formats application-specifically.
Assess difficulties during format changes and propose solutions.
Master direct modeling techniques and evaluate, select, and apply them in the context of usual history-based modeling strategies.
Know and master feature techniques up to UDFs (User-Defined-Features) and create and use them application-specifically.
Know the basics of Knowledge-Based-Engineering and implement own 'intelligent' models with appropriate techniques, especially parametrics.
Master the creation of freeform surfaces and bodies, sheet metal parts, assemblies, assembly families, and variants.
Develop these elements systematically and comprehensibly and use them in an application-adapted manner.
Evaluate corresponding elements and their use and make suggestions for improvement.
Master the terms from the CAx field, especially CAD-CAM, FEM, MKS, topology optimization, CFD, Digital Twin, CAS-Rendering, Rapid Prototyping, Animation, and VR/AR.
Develop models for the respective CAx strategies from CAD data, recognize and avoid errors.
Know the repercussions on the model structure in CAD resulting from the use of CAx techniques.
Generate simple CNC programs from CAD models using CAD-CAM, create FEM and MKS simulations, and evaluate their results.
Create renderings from CAD models.
Master the use of a PLM system, the associated terms, and classify, evaluate, and purposefully apply various PLM application strategies.
Work synchronously in a group on CAD models with the help of a PLM system.

syllabus_topics: Volume modeling including reference geometry, CSG, B-Rep and Sweeping
Fundamentals of CAD program structure, program parts and mathematical-algorithmic backgrounds
CAD interfaces, Reverse Engineering and Direct Modeling
Feature technology, User-Defined-Features and Knowledge-based Engineering
Modeling of Freeform Bodies and Surface Modeling
Assembly creation and generation and control of assembly families
Fundamentals of CAE-Simulation, FEM, MKS, Topology Optimization, CFD and Digital Twin regarding modeling strategy
CAS-Rendering, Animation and VR/AR techniques and effects on model structure
Rapid Prototyping in the CAD-modeling context
Data management and Product Lifecycle Management
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The grade's relevance for the final grade is determined by the study and examination regulations (SPO).
